0.long_answer: Bloom syndrome is a rare autosomal recessive disorder that is more commonly found in individuals of Ashkenazi Jewish descent. It is characterized by features such as short stature, photosensitivity, a predisposition to various cancers, and, in some cases, progeroid (premature aging) features. The disorder is caused by mutations in the BLM gene, which encodes a RecQ helicase enzyme. This protein plays a critical role in DNA repair and the maintenance of genomic stability. Mutations in the BLM gene result in an increased rate of chromosomal breakage and recombination, which contributes to the clinical manifestations and increased cancer risk observed in affected individuals.
